speaker: Patient
text: 24-year-old woman. The patient is in the postpartum period after delivering an 11 pound boy vaginally at 40 weeks gestation. She experienced a prolonged course during labor. She reports increased frequency of urination and uterine tenderness. She also mentions a decrease in bowel sounds.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Uterine tenderness. I also have Decreased bowel sounds, Increased frequency of urination, Fever. To keep my notes clear, please give only one final answer and keep it to a single direct conclusion.

speaker: Doctor
text: That uterine tenderness combined with fever and foul discharge is highly concerning for a postpartum infection. Has the fever spiked to over 101°F (38.3°C) within the last 24 hours? REQUEST TEST: CRP, Lactate.

speaker: Doctor
text: The pending inflammatory markers will confirm the severity, but the presence of decreased bowel sounds alongside uterine tenderness is a critical finding. Can you tell me if you have experienced any abdominal distension or difficulty passing stool? REQUEST IMAGES: Abdominal_CT_with_contrast.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Uncomplicated pregnancy leading up to a vaginal delivery. No significant past medical or surgical history. Social history: Does not smoke, drink alcohol, or use illicit drugs. Lives with her partner.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Postpartum Endometritis with likely secondary pelvic inflammatory process.
